say: Scan the table, order from your phone, and the kitchen sees it instantly. No waiting for a waiter. Restaurants pay real money for this, and today we start building it, with A.I.
This is a real project I'm building for restaurants. By the end of part one, orders from a phone will land in a live database, tagged with the right table.

heading: 3 parts, one at a time
items: Part 3: menu editor for the owner
say: Big projects fail when you ask A.I. for everything at once. So I split this into three parts, and build one at a time. Today, the customer side.
The key idea. Each table gets its own Q R code, with the table number inside the link. Table four's code opens the menu with table equals four. That's how the kitchen knows where to bring the food.

heading: Firebase setup, slowly
items: Add a web app, copy the config
Turn on Firestore in test mode (for now)
say: Firebase confuses a lot of people. It confused me too. So, slowly. Create a Firebase project. Add a web app, and copy the config. Turn on Firestore in test mode, just for now.

small: We lock it before the end
say: Remember those words, test mode. In test mode, anyone can read and write your data. We fix that before the end.

small: Subscribe for Part 2: the live kitchen screen
say: This is a series. Subscribe so you catch part two, where we build the kitchen screen.

lines: Build a mobile-first menu page in React with Tailwind. Read the table number from the URL. Load menu items from a Firestore collection called menu: name, price in Tanzanian shillings, category, description. Group by category. Add to cart, change quantity, and a sticky cart bar with the total. Plan first.
say: Now the menu page. Mobile first, React and Tailwind. Read the table number from the link. Load the menu from a Firestore collection, with prices in Tanzanian shillings. Group by category, add to cart, and a sticky cart bar with the total. Plan first.
I seed it with real dishes. Chips mayai, pilau, nyama choma, chapati, fresh juice, and ginger chai. And here's the menu, for table four.
Add two chips mayai, and a passion juice. The cart bar updates with the total.

small: Until the order actually goes somewhere
say: The menu looks great. But it's not a system, until the order actually goes somewhere. That's next. And then, the security mistake most tutorials leave in.

lines: When the customer taps Place order, save it to an orders collection with table number, items, total, status 'new' and a timestamp. Show a confirmation screen.
say: I ask Claude Code. When the customer taps place order, save it to an orders collection, with the table number, items, total, a status of new, and the time. Then show a confirmation screen.
Tap place order. Order sent to the kitchen.
And in the database, there it is. Table four. Two chips mayai, one juice. Status, new.

lines: Generate a printable page with QR codes for tables 1 to 10, each linking to the menu with its table number.
say: Now the Q R codes. One prompt. Generate a printable page, with codes for tables one to ten, each linking to the menu with its table number.
Print it, cut them out, and stick one on each table.

lines: Write Firestore security rules: anyone can read the menu and create an order, but nobody can edit or delete orders from the customer app.
say: Now, the fix I promised. Test mode lets anyone delete your orders. So I ask for security rules. Anyone can read the menu and create an order, but nobody can edit or delete orders from the customer app.

heading: Part 1 done
items: Table number lives in the QR link
say: Part one, done. The table number lives in the Q R link. The menu loads from Firestore. Orders are saved with the table and status. And the database is locked.
